subject: English
title: Class 10 English Olympiad — Paper 4
instructions: The time allowed for this paper is 60 minutes.
This paper contains 50 objective-type (multiple-choice) questions carrying a total of 60 marks.
There is no negative marking for wrong answers.
Each question has four options; choose the one correct answer.
Section 1 and other regular sections carry 1 mark per question; the Achievers Section carries 3 marks per question.
Use of calculators is not permitted unless specified.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: She is allergic ___ peanuts.
Fill in the blank with the correct article: He is ___ honest man.
Choose the correct plural form of 'phenomenon'.
Choose the word closest in meaning to 'meticulous'.
Identify the correct sentence.
options: He is one of the student who have passed the exam.
He are one of the students who has passed the exam.
He is one of the students who has passed the exam.
He is one of the students who have passed the exam.

questions.question: Identify the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: My favourite subjects are: Science, Mathematics, and English.
My favourite subjects are; Science, Mathematics, and English
My favourite subjects are, Science Mathematics and English.
My favourite subjects are Science; Mathematics, and English.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled word.
Choose the antonym of 'benevolent'.
Choose the word closest in meaning to 'ambiguous'.
Identify the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Where are you going she asked.
Where are you going, she asked?

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Hardly had she left ___ the phone rang.
Identify the correctly written sentence.
options: Neither of the boys has done their homework.
Neither of the boys have done his homework.
Neither of the boys has done his homework.
Neither of the boys have done their homework.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
Fill in the blank: She has been living here ___ 2015.
Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: She sings 'beautifully'.
Fill in the blank: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.
Choose the meaning of the idiom 'to let the cat out of the bag'.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He is good ___ mathematics.
Choose the correct conjunction: She was tired, ___ she kept working.
Choose the meaning of the idiom 'to bite the bullet'.
options: To face a difficult situation bravely

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The committee ___ meeting today at 5 pm.
Choose the correct word: The news ___ surprising.
Choose the synonym of 'candid'.
Fill in the blank with the correct modal: You ___ see a doctor if the pain continues.
Identify the correct reported speech: She said, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
options: She said that she calls me tomorrow.
She said I will call you tomorrow.
She said that she will call me tomorrow.
She said that she would call me the next day.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The detective's ___ helped solve the mystery.
Choose the correct comparative form: This is the ___ book of the two.
Identify the correctly formed question tag: She is coming, ___?
Choose the antonym of 'diligent'.
Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I am tired.'
options: He said that he is tired.
He said that he will be tired.
He said that I am tired.
He said that he was tired.

questions.question: Read: 'Despite winning the championship, the team's captain insisted on crediting every single player, saying victory was never a solo effort.' What quality does the captain display?
Read: 'After weeks of drought, the first drops of rain brought the entire village out onto the streets, dancing and cheering.' What does the villagers' reaction reveal?
options: Relief and joy after a long period of hardship caused by the drought

questions.question: Read: 'The museum's newest exhibit uses interactive holograms to let visitors 'walk through' ancient history.' What is unique about this exhibit?
options: It uses interactive holograms for an immersive experience

questions.question: Read: 'Even though the power went out during the storm, the family gathered around candlelight, sharing stories and laughing more than they had in months.' What is the underlying theme of this passage?
options: Unexpected hardships can bring people closer together

questions.question: Read: 'The librarian noticed that the same worn, dog-eared book kept disappearing and reappearing on the shelf, until she realized a young boy read it every day after school but always returned it before closing time.' What can be inferred about the boy?
options: He loved the book and was careful to return it responsibly

questions.question: Read: 'The bridge, once thought impossible to build across the roaring river, now stands as a symbol of the engineers' determination and skill.' What does the bridge symbolize?
options: Human determination and engineering achievement against difficulty

questions.question: Read: 'Rina loved painting but had never shown her work to anyone. One day, her teacher secretly submitted one of her paintings to a competition, and Rina won first prize.' Why was Rina surprised?
options: She hadn't shown her work to anyone and didn't know it was submitted
She had entered the competition herself

questions.question: Read: 'Though the two brothers often argued, they always stood by each other in times of trouble.' What does this suggest about their relationship?
options: Despite disagreements, their bond remained strong
They were not related by blood

questions.question: Read: 'The young inventor's device failed nine times before finally working on the tenth attempt, proving that persistence pays off.' What lesson does this passage convey?
options: Failure means one should stop trying
Inventions always work on the first try
Persistence and not giving up leads to eventual success
Luck is more important than effort

questions.question: Read: 'The old lighthouse had stood on the cliff for over a hundred years, guiding ships safely to shore even during the fiercest storms.' What is the main function of the lighthouse described here?
options: Guiding ships safely, especially during storms

questions.question: Read: 'The chef refused to use a single recipe twice, insisting that true creativity meant reinventing a dish every time it was cooked.' What trait best describes the chef?
Read: 'Maya's grandmother often said that patience was the key to happiness. Years later, Maya finally understood what she meant.' What can be inferred about Maya?
options: She became impatient as she grew older
She never thought about her grandmother's advice
She gained understanding or wisdom about patience over time

questions.question: Read: 'Despite the heavy rain, the farmers worked tirelessly in the fields, knowing that the monsoon was essential for their crops.' What does this passage suggest about the farmers' attitude?
options: They valued the rain despite the hardship it caused them
They were indifferent to the weather
They stopped working because of the rain

questions.question: Read: 'The scientist spent decades researching a cure, facing failure after failure, but she never gave up.' Which word best describes the scientist?
Read: 'As the sun set behind the mountains, the village slowly came alive with lanterns and the sound of laughter.' What time of day does this passage describe transitioning into?
Choose the sentence that best demonstrates effective use of a metaphor.
options: 'Time is a thief that steals our moments.'

questions.question: Identify the tone of this sentence: 'Oh wonderful, another Monday morning meeting.'
Which of these best demonstrates a well-structured argumentative statement with reasoning?
options: 'Schools should start later because I don't like waking up early.'
'Schools should start later because research shows teenagers need more sleep for better focus.'

questions.question: A student is asked to summarize a long article in one sentence while retaining its core meaning. Which skill is being tested?
options: Concise synthesis of the main idea

questions.question: Read the two statements: (1) 'He never lies.' (2) 'He always tells the truth.' What is the relationship between these two statements?
options: They express the same idea in different words
